sections.h2: Interior painting that looks good in Florida light
body: Florida sun is hard on interior walls in a way people do not expect. Big sliding doors and south-facing windows throw low afternoon light across the drywall, and every bad patch, roller mark, or flashed spot shows up. Good interior painting in Gainesville comes down to the work you do before the paint: patching, sanding, priming, and checking each wall under a raking light so the problems are fixed instead of hidden.

We paint living rooms, bedrooms, kitchens, bathrooms, hallways, stairwells, ceilings, trim, and interior doors for homeowners across Alachua and Marion counties. Our crews are our own employees, and the crew lead who walks your house is the one who runs the job.

sections.h2: Prep steps on every interior job
body: Interior prep is mostly about protection and repair. Floors are covered, furniture is moved and wrapped, and outlet covers and hardware come off. Then the wall work starts. If you are dealing with blisters or cracking, our guide to fixing bubbling drywall paint explains why that happens in humid homes and how we correct it.
bullets: Cover floors and move, wrap, and protect furniture
Patch holes, cracks, and nail pops, and match the wall texture
Sand patches smooth and check walls under a raking light
Caulk trim gaps and spot-prime patches and stains
Cut in ceilings and corners by hand rather than relying on tape
Two finish coats, with a third for major color changes

sections.h2: Picking the right sheen for each room
body: Sheen matters as much as color in a Florida house. Bathrooms and laundry rooms deal with steam and condensation, so they get a washable satin or semi-gloss. Hallways and kids' rooms get a scrubbable finish that can handle hands and backpacks. Living rooms with big windows usually look best in matte or eggshell, which hides small flaws in the drywall. Trim and doors get a harder enamel that holds up to cleaning. Our post on choosing a paint finish for any room goes further, room by room.

If color is the harder decision, our interior painting with color consultation package builds the palette into the project. We bring full-size drawdowns so you can see the color on your own wall before we order paint.

sections.h2: Ceilings, drywall, and the problems that show up first
body: Ceilings are where you spot water stains, hairline cracks along tape joints, and old popcorn texture. Stains get a stain-blocking primer so they do not bleed through the new coat. Larger drywall damage is handled through our drywall repair and patching service, and textured ceilings can be scraped smooth with popcorn ceiling removal before paint.

We use low-VOC, low-odor interior paint from premium Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore lines. Most rooms can be used again the same day once the paint is dry to the touch, which matters when it is a bedroom or the only bathroom.

A single room usually takes one day. A whole-home interior takes three days to two weeks, depending on square footage, ceiling height, the amount of repair, and the number of colors. We set the order of rooms with you, so the kitchen or a home office is down for as little time as possible. Interiors can be painted in any season, which makes them a good summer project when exterior days are short. If you are planning around a move, a new baby, or holiday guests, tell us the date on the walkthrough and we will build the schedule backward from it.

Each job ends with a walkthrough you sign. Anything that is not right gets fixed before we close it out, and labelled touch-up paint stays with you. Homeowners in the city can see local details on our Gainesville interior painting page, and we cover Ocala and Marion County too.

faqs.q: How long does it take to paint one room?
faqs.a: Most single rooms take one day, including prep and two coats. Rooms with heavy drywall repair, tall ceilings, or a dramatic color change can take longer.

faqs.q: What paint sheen should I use in a Florida bathroom?
faqs.a: A washable satin or semi-gloss. Those finishes resist moisture from showers and can be wiped down without burnishing. Flat paint tends to absorb moisture and mark easily in bathrooms.

faqs.q: Can I stay in my house during interior painting?
faqs.a: Yes. We move and protect furniture, work room by room, and use low-VOC paint, so most families stay home throughout the job.

faqs.q: Do you paint ceilings and trim too?
faqs.a: Yes. Ceilings, baseboards, crown, window and door casings, and interior doors can all be included. The estimate lists each surface so you can see exactly what is covered.
